runs.note: prose drafted by a local language model (llama3.1, accepted on attempt 2 after the checks sent it back); every figure inserted by the engine, and the capital statement checked against the run
runs.summary: The recent news about a "Russian troops try to seize Chernobyl nuclear plant amid…", a geopolitical event with impact 9.9 on a one-to-ten scale, has triggered a stress test that ran on 24 Feb 2022 19:45 UTC. The scenario assumes market moves similar to those seen in the closest historical crises (Russia annexes Crimea, US-China trade war escalation, Attack on Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq facility), blended with the average of 19 earlier crises and scaled up for the event's impact. Under this scenario, the book would lose $374m (1.68% of its value), from $22.33bn to $21.95bn, primarily due to credit losses (ECL) on Sberbank of Russia and Gazprom PJSC borrowers. The CET1 ratio would go from 13.50% to 9.68%, which stays above the 9.5% requirement, with headroom of 18 bp.
